title: panel-flow-sizing — a panel is a div: auto height, fill width, a floor; right/bottom edges resize; right-click resets

set.request: these root demo panels, they don't have resize grips on the root panel? i'm thinking: panels should probably default to default "div" behavior - auto-height, fill width... you could give a panel a min-height to prevent it from collapsing. but, the edges should still have resize handles. maybe for a default situation, the top and left resize handles aren't useful (they wouldn't work properly anyway), but right and bottom? also, right click should reset the resize handle's effect. that way, for any panel in "flow", adding a panel or section or content within should automatically grow the panel(s) themselves, not just crop/scroll
steps: read the sizing stack (size.js/css, split.js/css, Panel.js, panel.css, demo/page.js)
default = flow: h hug + a --panel-min floor
workspace height follows a hugging root
adding inside grows: unzero the flex chain
edge handles: drag = resize, right-click = reset (right/bottom only)
docs: sizing.md, decisions.md, readme, doc/file de-stale
set.outcome:
**A panel is a `div` in flow — and its right and bottom edges now size it.** [doc/sizing.md](/framework/ext/Panel/doc/sizing/) · [decisions](/framework/ext/Panel/doc/decisions/) · [Demo](/framework/ext/Panel/demo/) · [Panel](/framework/ext/Panel/)

`Panel.defaults.h` is **`hug`**: a panel's height is what it holds, never below **`--panel-min: 5em`**, and its width fills. Adding a split, a section or more text **grows** the panel and its hugging ancestors instead of scrolling inside them. A workspace nobody gave a `--panel-height` follows its root, so the Demo panes are exactly as tall as the arrangement in them.

![](flow-grow.png)

Three rules carry it, not a new mechanism: `height: var(--panel-height, auto)` on the workspace; `align-self: var(--panel-self-y, stretch)` on the hugging cross axis, with `size.js` writing `--panel-self-*` **only when a panel chose a `self`**; and `flex-basis: auto` (keeping `--panel-grow`) for a hugging height. Every workspace that was given a height is unmoved to the pixel — editor 662, Workspace 241, playground 862, files 451.

**The right and bottom edge strips carry three gestures:** click = split (unchanged), **drag = resize** (≥ 4px, never a ghost), **right-click = reset** to the default word. The length is `em` of the panel's own font, to the quarter, so it survives a zoom and a 3440 screen. Measured: 576 → drag −200 → `w: fixed`, `w_at 25em`, 376px; right-click → `w: fill`, 576. Bottom edge +120 → `h_at 39.25em`, and the workspace followed.

![](edge-resize.png)

**A split now matches its own preview.** The owner's 33/33/33 is fixed: `split.js`'s commit halves the struck panel's own `grow` when the twin lands beside it, and gives 1/1 when it nests. 600px → 300/300 → **150/150/300**, and the ghost's rect equals the arriving panel's rect exactly. The bar's `+` is `add`, not a split, and still reads 200/200/200. Flat halving beat nesting: no tree depth, seams stay peers, grows survive the chrome as `flex: n`.

Two traps cost a measurement each: `min(var(--panel-h-at), 100%)` resolves to **zero** against an auto-height workspace (a fixed root read 0px — the block axis uses `max-block-size: 100%` now), and the new `--panel-min` floor tied on specificity with `--panel-section` and won by load order (the playground's sections fell 241 → 75).

**Left, both named in decisions:** a root that is already a *split* still has no edge strips — `workspace.js` builds them leaf-only, and a split's strips lie over its children, which own the hover; and the ghost is a *side*, not a height, for a vertical split of a hugging panel, because the arriving section measures itself.

Zero console errors on nine pages plus the doc pages; `/data/panels.json` never written.
